subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Benford's Law in Fraud Detection
description: A quick win: understand Benford's Law in Fraud Detection.

hook.text: In natural data sets, the digit 1 appears first about 30% of the time. Fabricated numbers don't follow this pattern.

buildup.text: Benford's Law describes the expected distribution of first digits in naturally occurring number sets.

discovery.text: Auditors use Benford's Law to flag financial data that looks artificial — a sign of manipulation.

twist.text: Humans fabricating numbers tend to use too many 5s and 6s. The pattern is a mathematical fingerprint of fraud.

climax.text: Benford's Law turns math into a lie detector. Numbers that don't follow nature's pattern deserve scrutiny.

punchline.text: Fake numbers don't follow natural patterns. Math catches liars.

quiz.question: What does Benford's Law predict?
options: The distribution of first digits in natural data sets
The probability of fraud in any company
The maximum fine for financial crimes
